question: To support the European defence industry, the Commission announced new measures in the Strategic Compass that were intended to encourage joint procurement and projects. One of the initiatives announced was a proposal for a VAT waiver so as to encourage joint procurement of defence equipment. In addition, proposals for new financing solutions were also to be put forward. 1.
The Commission undertook to put forward a VAT waiver proposal by early 2023. Can it provide an update on this?
What is the status of the proposals for new financing solutions that were announced?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.4.2024) In her speech on the State of the European Union on 15 September 20211, the President of the Commission announced that the Commission would consider waiving value added tax (VAT) when buying defence equipment developed and produced in Europe in order to increase interoperability among Member States’ armed forces.

This proposal builds on the May 2022 Joint Communication on Defence Investment Gaps Analysis and Way Forward2. On 5 March 2024, the Commission put forward a proposal for a European Defence Industry Programme (EDIP) regulation3.

This proposal foresees a new legal framework, the Structure for European Armament Programme (SEAP)4, to underpin and strengthen defence cooperation, including in the context of projects under the Permanent Structured Cooperation (PESCO)5 if so agreed by Member States, in line with the European Defence Industrial Strategy6.
A cooperation under the SEAP could allow Member States, under certain conditions, to benefit from a VAT exemption where they jointly procure and own defence capabilities.
